profile.address: Renforsin Ranta Business Park, Kajaani, Finland
profile.reading: This is LUMI, one of Europes fastest supercomputers, housed in a converted former UPM paper mill hall at the Renforsin Ranta Business Park in Kajaani, Finland, within the same Kajaani Data Center Ecosystem industrial site as CSCs other Kajaani facility, though in its own separate building. Construction began in February 2020 and the data center building itself was completed in spring 2021, with LUMI formally inaugurated on June 13, 2022, after which it became the fastest supercomputer in Europe by early 2023. The system is an HPE Cray EX machine built around 10,240 AMD Radeon Instinct MI250X GPUs paired with AMD EPYC CPUs, totaling 362,496 CPU cores, 1.75 petabytes of RAM, and 117 petabytes of storage with 2 terabytes per second of aggregate input output bandwidth, delivering roughly 379 to 380 petaflops of sustained performance and about 531 petaflops peak, keeping it ranked among the worlds top 10 systems on the TOP500 list as of mid-2025. LUMI itself occupies a compact roughly 150 square meter footprint within CSCs much larger reserved hall space at the site, which runs about 2,200 square meters and is expandable to 4,600 square meters for future growth. The system draws about 7.1 megawatts of power, sourced entirely from hydroelectric generation, and its waste heat is fed into Kajaanis district heating network, reportedly supplying roughly a fifth of the citys heating needs. LUMI is owned jointly by the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking and an 11 nation LUMI Consortium comprising Finland, Belgium, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Iceland, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Sweden, and Switzerland, funded at a total budget of roughly 144.5 million euros split evenly between EuroHPC and the consortium, and is operated on their behalf by CSC, Finlands IT Center for Science. The system supports European scientific and AI research spanning physics, large language models, molecular dynamics, and climate modeling, and serves as a key computing platform for the European Unions Destination Earth digital twin initiative.
